Enteric duplication; respiratory failure, cord malformations and rib defects reported at 80-99%; cardiac abnormalities omitted because of cap.
Sensory/autonomic neuropathy with defining intestinal dysmotility; sweating is not skin damage, and fractures result from injury.
Severe junctional skin fragility; oral mucosal blistering in 2/2 patients supports gastrointestinal involvement.
Neoplasm originates in nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses, both within the airway axis; lymphoma is only one possible subtype.
Autoimmune destruction of small-intestinal villi; anemia and osteoporosis are separately diagnosed consequences of malabsorption.
Mixed silica and iron-dust pneumoconiosis directly affects pulmonary tissue.
Variable multiorgan failure commonly affects respiration, kidneys and circulation; coagulation dysfunction occurs in roughly 30% or more; hepatic/CNS dysfunction omitted by cap.
Benign urothelial neoplasm of the urinary tract, including bladder, ureter, renal pelvis or urethra.
Genetically mediated generalized epilepsy is a disorder of brain function.
Rectal mucosal ischemia and ulceration define the disease; anemia occurs in only 5-29%.
Defined as a connective-tissue soft-tissue neoplasm; neural designation alone does not establish nervous-system involvement.
Developmental delay, intellectual disability and microcephaly define the syndrome; split hand occurs in 80-99% and radial hypoplasia in 30-79%.
A superficial corneal dystrophy, localized to the eye.
Epithelial neoplasm originates in the rectum.
Red-cell aplasia; hearing impairment/external canal atresia, ventricular septal defect and cleft palate each reported in 2/4 patients; renal anomalies below 30%.
Congenital absence of cerebral white matter with intellectual disability directly affects the brain.
Inherited renal glucose-transport defect causes persistent glucosuria; systemic glucose regulation is preserved and other complications are uncommon.
Chronic mast-cell-mediated urticaria is an immune-mediated skin disorder; no common additional organ damage is established.
Inherited spasticity and ataxia define neurological dysfunction; additional organs vary by subtype.
Tessier 6 cleft involves the maxillozygomatic facial skeleton and characteristic lateral lower-eyelid defects.
Umbrella neurodevelopmental disorder defined by intellectual disability and developmental delay; other organ abnormalities vary across subtypes.
Nonsyndromic inherited intellectual disability; no evidence establishes a systemic metabolic disorder or additional organ damage.
Primary innate immunodeficiency; meningitis in 5/9 is a separately diagnosed infection, and skin infections occur in only 2/9.
Neurocutaneous syndrome with defining cardiac defects; scoliosis 9/22 and pectus excavatum 4/8 support skeletal involvement; bleeding and eyelid abnormalities omitted by cap.
